title: docs(permissions): give the real reason the invitation role cap guards the acceptance path
body:
Fixes #23323

Clause-②: no (docs)

## What changed

One paragraph of `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`: the invitation role-cap paragraph (lines 184-186 on `main`). Nothing else on this page or any other page.

The old sentence said `sys_member` is not one of the delegated-admin gate's governed objects. The gate does list it, and the same page says so twice: the governed-table list in "What the runtime gate enforces" and the gate table's "Membership is not delegable" row. The conclusion was right and stays. Only the reason changes.

Before:

> `sys_member` is not one of the gate's governed objects and the acceptance write runs outside the issuer's context, so the cap is the defense on that path.

After:

> `sys_member` *is* one of the gate's governed objects (the "Membership is not delegable" rule above), but the acceptance write never reaches the gate: better-auth writes the membership row as the system (`isSystem`), and the security middleware passes a system write through before the gate runs. So the cap — judged at issuance, while the inviter is still the actor — is the defense on that path.

## Each claim, checked against the code at the dispatch head `14a13bce06`

The four framework source files cited below are unchanged between `14a13bce06` and this PR's head, so the line numbers hold at both.

| Claim in the new sentence | Where the code says it |
|---|---|
| `sys_member` is a governed object | `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts:131-149`: `GOVERNED_OBJECTS` lists `'sys_member'` at `:148`. `assert()` returns early only for an object outside that set (`:284`). |
| A non-tenant-admin write to it is refused (the table row) | Same file, `:350-358`: `if (opCtx.object === 'sys_member')` throws `PermissionDeniedError`. |
| The gate does not judge a system write | Same file: the comment at `:142-144` ("every writer is a better-auth path running under `isSystem`, short-circuited before this gate") and the header at `:35-37`. The short-circuit itself is in the security middleware that calls the gate: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:2365-2367` (`if (opCtx.context?.isSystem) return next();`) runs before `this.delegatedAdminGate.assert(opCtx)` at `:2554-2556`. Both are in the one middleware registered at `:2319`. |
| The acceptance write runs as the system | better-auth `1.7.3`, `dist/plugins/organization/routes/crud-invites.mjs:324`, calls `adapter.createMember(...)`. That reaches the framework adapter's `create` in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts:883-884` (`adoptExistingMembership` or `dataEngine.insert`). There `dataEngine = withSystemContext(rawDataEngine)` (`:755`), and its `insert` injects `isSystem: true` (`:704`, `:707`). |
| The cap is judged at issuance, while the inviter is the actor | `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:3262-3279`: the `beforeCreateInvitation` hook calls `invitationRoleCapFailure(...)`. |

The citations are here and not in the docs sentence because the page cites no source files anywhere, only dogfood tests. A source line number in a docs page goes stale as soon as the file is edited.

I ran them after building `@objectstack/spec` and the production closure of `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/client-react`. A first pass before those builds exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). That pass measured nothing and is not counted.

The same lane's `node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs` (with `--self-test`) exits 0.
- MDX compile: the page compiled with the docs app's own `@mdx-js/mdx` (the copy `fumadocs-mdx` resolves) plus `remark-gfm`. The before and after versions both compile. A negative control (an unclosed expression planted in the same file) fails to compile, which shows the compiler can catch an error. The full `next build` (CI's Build Docs job) was not run locally and is left to CI.

## `skip-changeset`

No published package ships `content/docs/**`. I read the `files[]` of all 71 non-private workspace packages: none names a `content` or `docs` path. Then I grepped the 131 existing `files[]` roots after the build:

- 0 hits for the old sentence and 0 for the new one.
- Positive control: `adminScope` hits 64 shipped files, 32 of them under `packages/spec/dist`. So the scan does reach built shipped output.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-cap.ts:22-25` (header comment) still gives the stale reason: "`DelegatedAdminGate`'s `GOVERNED_OBJECTS` does not cover `sys_member`, and the acceptance-time membership write runs under better-auth's own context". It is the same wrong reason this PR fixes in the docs, and it was probably where the docs sentence came from. I left it alone for two reasons. The claim limits this diff to the one docs paragraph. And editing a `plugin-auth` source file would widen the gate set beyond the docs families. It is a code comment, so it is not a filing class. Carrier: none.
- The released `CHANGELOG.md` entries in `plugin-auth`, `spec`, `lint` and `platform-objects` say "`sys_member` is not a `GOVERNED_OBJECT`". That was true when they shipped, and those files are release-owned, so they are not touched.
